claim: For every finite set D of distinct integers d >= 3 with gcd(D)=1 and sum_{d in D} 1/(d-1)>=1, every integer k>=1, and every finite set F of labelled occurrences (d,j) with d in D and j>=k, list the occurrences outside F by increasing value and then increasing base label as a_1,a_2,... and set S_m=sum_{i=1}^m a_i; there exist integers L>=0 and m_0>=1 such that, for every m>=m_0, every integer n in [L,S_m-L] is a subset sum of a_1,...,a_m, with each occurrence used at most once.

quadruple.statement: Candidate C2, unproved: for every D,k,F in the admitted C1 claim, there exist integers L>=0 and m>=1 such that a_{m+1} exceeds every deleted value, S_m>=2L, every integer in [L,S_m-L] is a subset sum of the first m remaining occurrences, and S_r-a_{r+1}>=2L-1 for every r>=m; both L and m are chosen together and may depend on D,k,F.
quadruple.stage: Labelled finite subset sums of integer geometric streams, ordered by numerical value with repeated occurrences retained.

shape.objects: An infinite ordered sequence of labelled pure-power occurrences after a finite deletion, its finite prefixes, and their finite subset-sum sets. Prefixes extend by appending unused occurrences. Finset, Nat powers, List, order and sums are core Lean or Mathlib objects.
shape.quantifiers: For every admissible finite D, every positive k and every finite F, there exist L and m_0, for every m>=m_0 and integer n in [L,S_m-L], there exists I subset of {1,...,m} with n=sum_{i in I}a_i.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-coverage decision; an unspecified threshold N(D,k) suffices, and no explicit numerical optimum is requested.
shape.ambient_structure: Integer order and modular arithmetic coexist. Adding an unused occurrence replaces a finite subset-sum set T by T union (T+a), preserving occurrence uniqueness. This recursion propagates a represented interval when its length is at least the next occurrence.
shape.symmetries: Base relabelling and complement symmetry T_m=S_m-T_m preserve prefix subset sums. Common dilation changes the integer lattice. No invariant structured-piece intersection family is recorded.
shape.configuration: For every sufficiently long prefix, every integer in its central interval [L,S_m-L] must be represented using that prefix, each occurrence once. Restricting a represented prefix to a shorter prefix or deleting its low powers can destroy its central interval. Quantification over all finite F permits new L and m_0 after deletion, not preservation of a particular old interval.
shape.extremal_candidate: No counterexample to C1 is known. Pure powers of 2 illustrate the danger of generic finite deletion but do not satisfy the admitted hypotheses.
shape.finite_certificates: Membership of a specified n in a specified prefix has a finite witness or exhaustive check. C1 and its negation quantify over unbounded prefixes and thresholds, so neither has a known complete finite certificate. A seed alone is not a tail proof. Small interval operations can be checked by hand or solver.
shape.monotonicity: For a fixed prefix total, increasing L shrinks the required interval; for C1, increasing m_0 weakens the conclusion. The all-positive-cutoff claim remains open at k=1. Monotonicity under arbitrary addition of bases is not assumed because the upper endpoint S_m also changes.
shape.uniformity_parameter: For every fixed D,k and finite F, L is independent of the prefix m. No effective common L across different D,k,F is requested.
shape.proof_shape: Candidate C1 states every quantifier explicitly. The proposed proof is induction in prefix length with invariant [L,S_m-L] contained in T_m. The elementary append operation requires a_next <= S_m-2L+1 and then preserves L. The actual seed and all-future inequality are not proved. The stopped Brown-type methods control total capacity and this append operation, not seed production.
shape.neighbours: Known true: Brown interval extension with its explicit length condition; the root move's elementary implication C1 implies eventual completeness; bounded-gap and disjoint-supply completeness theorems in BEGL96 and Bergelson-Simmons. Known false: arbitrary finite deletion preserves completeness (powers of 2); abstract syndetic finite-sum completeness in the examples of Bergelson-Simmons. Open here: C1, C2 and the original pure-power conjecture. Candidate G, unproved: for locally finite nondecreasing labelled positive-integer sequences of bounded multiplicity, divergent prefix surplus, gcd one in every tail, divergent squared irrational distances for every irrational, and raw label exponent greater than one imply eventual central-prefix coverage. G drops pure-power structure and tests only a proposed source of C2 seeds; no assertion that all root instances already satisfy its hypotheses is made.
shape.known_bounds: Brown-type extension provides central coverage only conditional on a seed and every subsequent length inequality. BEGL96 and Bergelson-Simmons distinguish bounded gaps from cofiniteness. C1 has no identified complete proof, bounded counterexample domain, finite reduction, or first-moment theorem establishing the target. This inherits the root's documented ceiling, not a new claim that C1 was historically studied by name.
shape.missing_input: Two distinct requirements remain: a represented seed interval with controlled endpoint loss, and the sufficient extension inequality at every subsequent prefix. No single known conjecture or input has been shown to settle both.
shape.base_theory: Classical number theory in ZFC, with finite and countable objects only; no independence or extra set-theoretic axiom is known or proposed. Elementary finite verification and the intended proofs lie within Lean's standard classical axioms when formalized.

known: Aristotle/Alexeev: all nonnegative n at cutoff 0 by Brown induction; https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos124b.lean.
BEGL96: positive-density infinite bases yield cutoff-dependent finite complete subsets; cutoff-1 examples and interval-base estimates on p.137; DOI 10.4064/aa-77-2-133-138.

Bergelson-Simmons: bounded prefix deficit implies syndetic finite sums, and Theorem 1.23 gives strong completeness with three disjoint reciprocal blocks and a gcd-one supply; arXiv:1507.02208v2, DOI 10.4064/aa8221-10-2016.

Root move 1, checkpoint-000001: C1 implies the original claim by taking F empty and choosing S_m>=n+L. This elementary argument is pending independent mathematical acceptance; C1 remains a hypothesis.
